prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

We search for stellar and substellar companions of young nearby stars to investigate stellar multiplicity and formation of stellar and substellar companions. We detect common proper-motion companions of stars via multi-epoch imaging. Their companionship is finally confirmed with photometry and spectroscopy. Here we report the discovery of a new co-moving (13 sigma) stellar companion ~17.8 arcsec (350 AU in projected separation) north of the nearby star HD141272 (21 pc). With EMMI/NTT optical spectroscopy we determined the spectral type of the companion to be M3+-0.5V. The derived spectral type as well as the near infrared photometry of the companion are both fully consistent with a 0.26+-0.07 Msol dwarf located at the distance of HD141272 (21 pc). Furthermore the photometry data rules out the pre-main sequence status, since the system is consistent with the ZAMS of the Pleiades.

outputs.L1:
We search for stellar and substellar companions to young, nearby stars in order to investigate stellar multiplicity and the formation of stellar and substellar companions. Common proper-motion companions are identified through multi-epoch imaging, with companionship ultimately confirmed by photometry and spectroscopy.

Here, we report the discovery of a new co-moving stellar companion at a significance of 13σ, located approximately 17.8 arcsec north of the nearby star HD 141272 (21 pc), corresponding to a projected separation of 350 AU. Using optical spectroscopy obtained with EMMI/NTT, we determined the companion’s spectral type to be M3 ± 0.5 V. This spectral classification, together with the companion’s near-infrared photometry, is fully consistent with a 0.26 ± 0.07 M⊙ dwarf located at the distance of HD 141272. Furthermore, the photometric data rule out a pre-main-sequence status, as the system is consistent with the zero-age main sequence of the Pleiades.
outputs.L2:
We investigate young stars in the solar neighborhood to identify stellar and substellar companions, with the aim of studying multiplicity and how such companions form. Candidate companions sharing the same proper motion are found through imaging obtained at multiple epochs, and their physical association is then verified using photometric and spectroscopic observations.

We present the discovery of a previously unknown stellar companion moving together with the nearby star HD141272, located at a distance of 21 pc. The companion is detected at a significance of 13 sigma and lies about 17.8 arcseconds north of the primary star, corresponding to a projected separation of roughly 350 AU. Optical spectra obtained with EMMI on the NTT show that the companion has a spectral classification of M3 ± 0.5 V. This spectral type, together with its near-infrared photometry, agrees well with a dwarf star of mass 0.26 ± 0.07 solar masses situated at the same distance as HD141272. In addition, the photometric measurements exclude a pre-main-sequence nature, because the system is compatible with the zero-age main sequence of the Pleiades.
outputs.L3:
The study aims to identify stellar and substellar companions around young, nearby stars in order to better understand the frequency of multiplicity and the processes by which companions form. By surveying nearby young systems, the work helps place constraints on how often stars host low-mass stellar or substellar companions and how such companions are distributed at wide separations.

Candidate companions are identified primarily through multi-epoch imaging. Objects that share the same proper motion as the target star are considered likely physically associated companions, rather than unrelated background sources. These common proper-motion candidates are then further examined using photometric and spectroscopic observations, which allow their physical properties and association with the primary star to be tested more robustly.

As part of this survey, a new co-moving stellar companion was discovered near the star HD 141272. The companion lies approximately 17.8 arcseconds to the north of the primary, corresponding to a projected physical separation of about 350 AU at the distance of the system. Its common proper motion indicates that it is gravitationally associated with HD 141272 rather than being a chance alignment with a background object.

Follow-up optical spectroscopy was obtained using EMMI on the New Technology Telescope. These observations showed that the companion has a spectral type of M3±0.5V, identifying it as a main-sequence M dwarf. This classification is supported by its spectral features and by comparison with standard stellar templates.

The companion’s spectral type, together with its near-infrared photometry, is consistent with a low-mass dwarf of approximately 0.26±0.07 solar masses located at a distance of about 21 pc. The available photometric and spectroscopic evidence does not support a pre-main-sequence nature for the object. Instead, the data indicate that the companion is a main-sequence M dwarf physically associated with HD 141272.
outputs.L4:
This study presents a search for stellar and substellar companions to young, nearby stars using high-resolution, multi-epoch imaging. The primary goal is to identify faint objects located close to target stars and determine whether they are physically associated companions or unrelated background sources. Candidate companions are first selected from imaging data and then tested through proper-motion analysis: objects that share the motion of the primary star across multiple observing epochs are considered likely bound companions. Follow-up photometric and spectroscopic observations are then used to characterize the confirmed candidates and estimate their physical properties, including spectral type, distance consistency, and mass.

As part of this survey, a new co-moving companion to the nearby star HD 141272 is reported. The object is found at a projected separation of approximately 350 AU from the primary star and exhibits common proper motion with it, strongly indicating that the two objects form a physical binary system rather than a chance alignment. Photometric measurements and spectroscopic classification show that the companion is an M3 ± 0.5 V dwarf. Its properties are consistent with a main-sequence star located at the same distance as HD 141272, about 21 pc from the Sun.

Based on the derived spectral type and luminosity, the companion is estimated to have a mass of approximately 0.26 ± 0.07 solar masses. This places it firmly in the low-mass stellar regime rather than among brown dwarfs or planetary-mass objects. The projected separation of 350 AU makes the system a relatively wide binary, providing a useful example of low-mass stellar companionship around nearby young stars.

The discovery of this companion adds to the census of nearby multiple-star systems and contributes to a broader understanding of stellar multiplicity, especially at wide separations and low companion masses. Such systems are important for studying the formation and dynamical evolution of binary and multiple stars, as well as for refining estimates of how common low-mass stellar companions are around nearby solar-type and young stars.

counterfactuals.output: We report the discovery of a co-moving stellar companion to the nearby star HD 141272. The companion lies at an angular separation of ∼7.6″, corresponding to a projected physical separation of ∼160 AU at the system distance of ∼21 pc. Multi-band optical and near-infrared photometry place the object on the main sequence at the distance of HD 141272 and indicate a late-M spectral type. Follow-up spectroscopy shows strong molecular absorption bands consistent with an M4–M5 dwarf, with no evidence for a background giant or extragalactic contaminant. Its luminosity and colors imply a mass of roughly 0.15–0.20 M⊙. counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a scientific abstract in the style of an astrophysics discovery note about a 13-sigma common proper-motion companion located 17.8 arcsec north of HD141272 at 21 pc.
counterfactuals.output: **Abstract** — We report the identification of a wide common proper-motion companion to the nearby star HD 141272. The source is located \(17.8^{\prime\prime}\) north of the primary, corresponding to a projected physical separation of \(\sim 374\) au at the system distance of 21 pc. Multi-epoch astrometry demonstrates that the object shares the proper motion of HD 141272 at a significance of \(13\sigma\), strongly rejecting the hypothesis of a stationary background contaminant. Its close astrometric agreement with the primary, combined with the low probability of a chance alignment at the measured separation, supports its interpretation as a gravitationally bound companion. The discovery adds HD 141272 to the population of nearby stellar systems hosting wide companions at several hundred astronomical units, providing a useful benchmark for studies of wide-binary formation, dynamical survival, and coeval low-mass stellar or substellar atmospheres. Further photometric and spectroscopic characterization will be required to determine the companion’s mass, spectral type, and evolutionary state.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a research-paper abstract for a survey searching for stellar and substellar companions to young nearby stars using multi-epoch imaging, with a specific discovery of an M3 ± 0.5 V companion to HD141272.
counterfactuals.output:
We present the results of a multi-epoch imaging survey designed to identify stellar and substellar companions to young, nearby stars. The survey targets stars with youth indicators and favorable distances for direct detection of low-mass companions at wide separations. Candidate companions were selected from deep imaging data and tested for physical association through common proper motion analysis using follow-up observations obtained at multiple epochs. Photometric measurements were used to estimate spectral types and to assess consistency with companionship at the distance and age of each primary.

As part of this survey, we report the discovery of a previously unrecognized companion to HD 141272. The object shares the proper motion of the primary within the astrometric uncertainties, ruling out a stationary background source and supporting a bound association. Its colors and absolute magnitude are consistent with a main-sequence M dwarf, for which we derive a spectral type of M3 ± 0.5 V. The companion therefore represents a low-mass stellar component rather than a substellar object. This discovery adds to the census of low-mass companions around young nearby stars and demonstrates the effectiveness of multi-epoch imaging for distinguishing physically associated companions from unrelated background objects. Our results contribute to constraints on the frequency and properties of wide stellar and substellar companions in young stellar populations.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose an astrophysical discovery report paragraph describing how photometry and spectroscopy confirm a 0.26 solar-mass dwarf companion at 350 AU projected separation from HD141272 and compare it to the Pleiades ZAMS.
counterfactuals.output: Deep imaging of HD 141272 reveals a faint comoving source at a projected separation of approximately 350 AU, whose broadband photometry is consistent with a low-mass main-sequence companion rather than a background object. Using the distance to the primary, the companion’s apparent magnitudes place it on the lower main sequence with colors characteristic of an early- to mid-M dwarf, implying a mass of about 0.26 M☉ from standard stellar-evolution mass–luminosity relations. Follow-up spectroscopy confirms this interpretation: the spectrum shows the molecular absorption bands and temperature-sensitive features expected for a cool dwarf, while lacking the signatures of a giant or extragalactic contaminant. When plotted on an absolute color–magnitude diagram, the object lies close to the Pleiades zero-age main sequence, indicating that its luminosity and color are consistent with a normal hydrogen-burning dwarf of comparable mass. Together, the photometric placement, spectroscopic dwarf classification, and physical association with HD 141272 confirm the object as a bound 0.26-solar-mass dwarf companion at wide separation.
